rca.rootCause: When a bytes value is assigned to a DataElement with VR 'OL' (or other O* VRs), pydicom incorrectly splits the bytes on the backslash byte (0x5C) and wraps the result in a MultiValue. This happens because the code that handles value assignment/conversion for byte-string VRs treats the backslash character as a DICOM value separator, even though byte/binary VRs (OB, OW, OF, OL, OD, etc.) should be stored as a single bytes object without any splitting. When the bytes value happens to contain 0x5C (backslash), it gets split into multiple byte fragments inside a MultiValue, which later causes 'TypeError: a bytes-like object is required, not MultiValue' during writing/serialization.
evidence: Issue title: 'Error : a bytes-like object is required, not MultiValue' when updating tag LongTrianglePointIndexList (0066,0040) with VR 'OL'
Reporter notes error only occurs with VR 'OL', works fine with 'OB', 'OF' etc.

Maintainer reproduces and observes: print(ds) shows the OL value split into a MultiValue of two byte fragments: [b'...\\x00[\\x00', b'\\x00]\\x00...'] — indicating the backslash byte 0x5C in the data triggered splitting
Maintainer comment: 'I think this is because the byte value is hitting the hex for the backslash character during assignment. Ouch, that's kinda nasty.'

The value conversion/assignment logic in pydicom/values.py and pydicom/dataelem.py is responsible for converting raw values and must avoid applying backslash-based MultiValue splitting to binary/byte VRs
